title: Decision-tree learning degree
statement: Let $T$ be a real-valued binary decision tree on $n$ coordinates, with an available set of coordinates, and let $\varepsilon$ be rational with $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$. Define its learning degree as the decision-tree truncation degree determined by the number of leaves of $T$ and the threshold $\varepsilon/2$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite available set of coordinates
A real-valued binary decision tree on that available set
